payload.title: The three policy rule ids are listed in the ESLint config, in POLICY_RULES, in the manifest and in the adapter test with no structural pin between the config's enabled rules and POLICY_RULES, so a fourth rule enabled in the config but missing from POLICY_RULES would be ranked by its plugin meta and judged under the generic contract while every test stays green.
evidence: tools/aria-adapters/lint-rules-adapter.ts:127-131 (POLICY_RULES, a second list of the same ids)
tools/aria-adapters/lint-rules-adapter.ts:133-139 (severity is lifted only for ids in POLICY_RULES, else taken from plugin meta)
tools/aria-adapters/lint-rules-adapter.tool.json:61-96 (a third list, one manifest entry per id)
tools/aria-adapters/lint-rules-adapter.test.ts:617-632 (the pin compares manifest keys with the fired rules filtered through the test's own copy)
payload.rule_violated: Single owner of one fact (CLAUDE.md Architectural Approach tier 2 or at least tier 3): the set of policy rules is derived once or pinned.
payload.notes: A fourth rule added to the config's policy block without editing POLICY_RULES, the manifest and the test fires in the scan, severityFor ranks it by its own meta (low for a suggestion rule), no per-rule contract exists so the judge applies the generic star contract, and the test stays green because its fired set is filtered through its own copy of the ids. Not reachable with the current three ids. Close condition: Add one test that reads the policy rules block of the config module and asserts its key set equals POLICY_RULES and the manifest's non-star keys, or derive POLICY_RULES from the config. Plan row: DET detector program (landing batch 3). Verified at origin/main d716541239.
